intro_screen_1_body: You have ◈60 and a roof you do not pay for. In five years someone will hand you a payslip and expect you to cope with it.
intro_screen_2_body: ◈4,000 by the time you are nineteen. No windfall, no lucky month — what the months leave behind.
intro_screen_3_body: You decide where the money goes before you know what the month holds. Then something happens, as it does. At the close you see what it cost.
intro_screen_3_footnote: Income lands when you start the month. The rest is up to you.
intro_privacy: Your progress is saved on this device with a random id. No name, no email, no tracking.
plan_subtitle: Put the money where you want it before the month gets a say.
plan_hint_body: The allowance stopped. This year, hours are the money.
plan_hint_note: Set them before the month starts.
plan_work_hours_hint: Set the hours the month will pay you for.
plan_saving_note: the part that buys your future
event_blocked: Not enough free time — you cannot borrow hours.
event_blocked_fund: Not enough in Savings — the Fund cannot borrow.
event_cascade_debt: The cascade: {from} came out of the Save envelope, and {to} went onto Debt.
event_cascade_save: The cascade: {from} came out of the Save envelope.
resolve_over_note: You went past one of your envelopes this month. That is allowed — the cascade covered it — but the money came from somewhere.
hud_life_stage_1: School, the bus pass, and evenings nobody has claimed yet.
hud_life_stage_2: School, a phone in your pocket, and a bill with your name on it.
hud_life_stage_3: School by day, shifts by evening, and fewer free nights.
hud_life_stage_4: The last year of school, and everyone asking what comes next.
hud_life_stage_5: School behind you, and a year with no timetable in it.
stage_2_beat: Fifteen. A phone bill in your own name, and a month that has to be planned.
stage_3_beat: Sixteen. The allowance stops; the hours start paying.
stage_4_beat: Seventeen. Credit arrives before the income to carry it.
stage_5_beat: Eighteen. School is behind you, and the money gets real.
stats_no_curve: The curve appears once a month has closed.
story_coverage: What the five years showed you
story_opening_debt: You started at 14 with {start} and finished at 19 with {final}, still owing {debt}.
story_opening_free: You started at 14 with {start} and finished at 19 with {final}, owing nothing.
story_adherence: You kept to the plan you set yourself in {months} of the 60 months.
story_band_ahead: You ended up past the goal you were aiming at, with the score to go with it.
story_band_treading: You ended up still moving — not ahead, and not sunk either.
story_band_behind: You ended up behind where you needed to be. The five years are on the record, exactly as they went.
story_band_note: your ending, from the money and the score
story_you_vs_you_note: Year one against year five. Nobody else's numbers.

match.monthsPlural=one: Your longest run inside your own budget was 1 month.
match.monthsPlural=other: Your longest run inside your own budget was {months} months.

story_inside_budget_none: No month closed inside your own budget this time — the plan and the month never quite agreed.
story_what_next_body: The Fork comes round again in month 49. Studying and working end very differently.
story_saved: This Run is saved to your profile — playing again starts from month 1.
story_offline: This Run could not be saved. Reload to try the finish again.
story_journal_body: Every finished Run is kept on your profile as a Chapter — its band, its Milestones, and the Concepts you have met across them.
journal_lead: Every finished Run, in the order you lived it — your Milestones, your Concepts, nobody else's numbers.
journal_empty_body: Finish a Run and it becomes the first Chapter here — in the order you lived it, never a ranking.
settings_lead: The game keeps one thing about you: a random id and the Run it points at. Take it with you or delete it — neither needs an account.
settings_download_body: A JSON file holding everything the game keeps: the Run in progress, if there is one, and every finished Run kept for replay — the month, the money, the plan and the choices.
settings_delete_body: Removes every stored Run — the one in progress and any finished ones — and clears the id on this device. It cannot be undone: a fresh Run starts from month 1.
settings_delete_error: That did not go through. Nothing was deleted — try again.
settings_language_body: The game speaks English, Italian and Romanian. Switching changes the words only — your Run and your progress stay exactly where they are.
settings_sound_body: Quiet cues on choices, month closes and the big moments. Off by default; nothing here needs sound to make sense.
settings_preview_note: Previews play even while sound is off; the setting stays where you left it.
privacy_heading: What the game knows about you.
privacy_lead: Short version: your progress, and nothing else.

milestone_half_year_inside_budget: Six months in a row inside budget

milestone_the_climb: Turned back up after three months down
flag_overdraft: Month {month}: you let the account go negative rather than wait.
flag_minimum_payment: Month {month}: you paid only the minimum, and the rest of the balance was spread over six months.
flag_card_issued: Month {month}: the card arrived, and with it a score to look after.
flag_fork_study: Month {month}: you chose to study, and the loan went on the sheet.
flag_fork_work: Month {month}: you chose to work, and paid a deposit on somewhere to live.
card_the_allowance_situation: Your parents sit you down. From now on you get ◈40 a month, and it is yours to get wrong. No top-ups.
card_the_allowance_choice_spend_label: Buy the thing you have been wanting
card_the_allowance_choice_spend_feedback: The first money costs no hours, and nothing is asking for it yet. Every hour you sell is an hour you cannot buy back.
card_the_allowance_choice_spend_reaction: The thing is yours. Forty is already gone.
card_the_allowance_choice_keep_label: Leave it where you cannot reach it
card_the_allowance_choice_keep_feedback: Still there at the end of the month, and the month did not have to think about it. Every hour you sell is an hour you cannot buy back.
card_the_allowance_choice_keep_reaction: Forty stays where you put it. The month ends with it still there.
card_two_wants_situation: The game you have waited months for is out, and the headphones you actually need for school are on sale. You can afford one, today.
card_two_wants_choice_game_feedback: You picked the one you wanted over the one you needed, and nothing breaks today. The headphones will still be needed next month; money you do not spend is the only money you keep.
card_two_wants_choice_game_reaction: The game is brilliant. The headphones are still in the shop.
card_two_wants_choice_headphones_feedbac: The boring one, and it was cheaper — the difference stayed in the envelope. Money you do not spend is the only money you keep.
card_two_wants_choice_headphones_reactio: The headphones are yours at the sale price. The game waits on the shelf.
card_odd_job_situation: Next door offers ◈30 to clear their garden this weekend. It is the whole weekend.
card_odd_job_choice_take_feedback: Fourteen hours for thirty. The first work you are paid for feels different from money someone handed you.
card_odd_job_choice_take_reaction: Two weekends gone. Thirty, in cash, in your hand.
card_odd_job_choice_pass_feedback: Nothing was lost and nothing was earned. The weekend cost no money and made none; both ledgers stayed level.
card_odd_job_choice_pass_reaction: The weekend stays yours. The neighbour finds somebody else for the garden.
card_birthday_gift_situation: Your best friend’s birthday is on Friday. You have nothing for them yet.
card_birthday_gift_choice_buy_label: Buy the gift everyone is chipping in for
card_birthday_gift_choice_buy_feedback: The Want envelope did its job: a real cost, planned with the group, still affordable on the day.
card_birthday_gift_choice_buy_reaction: Twenty-five leaves the Want envelope. The present is on the table on Friday.
card_birthday_gift_choice_make_feedback: It cost no money and it cost the evening. Both ledgers are real.
card_birthday_gift_choice_make_reaction: Six hours at the kitchen table, and a present the others did not buy.
card_birthday_gift_choice_skip_feedback: The money stayed put, and the evening went on without a present from you. The part that cost is not on any statement.
card_birthday_gift_choice_skip_reaction: You show up with nothing. Nobody mentions it, and the evening goes on.
card_phone_cracked_situation: It slipped out of your hand on the stairs. The screen is a spiderweb.
card_phone_cracked_choice_ack_feedback: A bill nobody planned for. The cover paid it, or the month’s money did — and where the month came up short, Save first, then Debt.
card_phone_cracked_choice_ack_reaction: The screen is a spiderweb. The repair shop wants its money.
card_insurance_offer_situation: Your phone is still in one piece — for now. Cover costs ◈6 a month.
card_insurance_offer_odds: About 1 in 3 of phones this age take a knock this year.
card_insurance_offer_choice_insure_feedb: Six a month, and the phone can break once without the repair landing on this month’s money. That is what the six bought.
card_insurance_offer_choice_risk_feedbac: The six stayed in the month and the odds went with you. Fine odds, until the repair is yours alone.
card_insurance_offer_choice_risk_reactio: The six stays in your pocket. The phone goes back in the same bag.
card_canteen_week_situation: The canteen takes about ◈5 a day. Packing lunch takes ten minutes each morning and costs about half as much.
card_canteen_week_choice_pack_feedback: Four hours a month for half the money. The part you paid in was the part you had spare.
card_canteen_week_choice_pack_reaction: Ten minutes in the kitchen every morning, and lunch comes from home.
card_canteen_week_choice_buy_feedback: Twenty-five a month for someone else to make lunch. By summer that is a bike, and not one sandwich will be remembered.
card_canteen_week_choice_buy_reaction: Lunch appears at the counter and the morning stays quiet.
card_dog_walking_situation: A woman two streets over needs her dog walked on school days. Three units a walk, every walk, in cash.
card_dog_walking_choice_take_feedback: Thirty a month for eight hours. Not much, and it is the first money nobody gave you.
card_dog_walking_choice_take_reaction: Three a walk, every walk, in cash. The dog waits at the gate on Monday.
card_dog_walking_choice_pass_feedback: No wages this month, and no mornings gone. The dog found somebody with earlier starts.
card_dog_walking_choice_pass_reaction: The mornings stay yours. Somebody else gets the thirty.
card_sell_games_situation: Twenty-three games, none of them played since last year. The trade-in app offers ◈45 for the lot.
card_sell_games_choice_sell_feedback: Forty-five for a drawer you had stopped opening. The money was already gone; this is a piece of it coming back.
card_sell_games_choice_sell_reaction: The drawer goes out in one box; forty-five comes in.
card_sell_games_choice_keep_feedback: Maybe. The drawer keeps the games; the games keep forty-five that could be somewhere else.
card_sell_games_choice_keep_reaction: The drawer stays shut. The trade-in app moves on to somebody else’s drawer.
card_bus_pass_situation: Your bus pass is not in any pocket. A replacement is ◈30, or you walk forty minutes each way until it turns up.
card_bus_pass_choice_replace_feedback: The walk was the other price, and this month thirty was cheaper than forty minutes twice a day.
card_bus_pass_choice_replace_reaction: Thirty, gone on a piece of plastic, and the bus is there tomorrow.
card_bus_pass_choice_walk_feedback: Twelve hours a month and sore shoes. The money would have been the cheaper price, and you paid in the other currency.
card_bus_pass_choice_walk_reaction: You walk it. Forty minutes each way, twice a day, and the money stays.
card_grandma_windfall_situation: A card arrives late with ◈50 inside and a note that says do not spend it all at once.
card_grandma_windfall_choice_save_feedba: The note asked for this, and the drawer was easy. Week one is where the fifty usually goes, and this one went nowhere.
card_grandma_windfall_choice_save_reacti: The fifty lands and stays folded in the drawer.
card_grandma_windfall_choice_treat_feedb: One treat, and thirty-five still saved. The mistake would be spending the fifty twice, not spending it once.
card_trip_deposit_situation: The school trip costs ◈60, due in two months. The first ◈20 holds your place until then.
card_trip_deposit_choice_deposit_feedbac: Twenty holds the place, and the other forty has two months and a reason to arrive.
card_trip_deposit_choice_deposit_reactio: Twenty holds the place. The trip has a date now, and so does the money.
card_trip_deposit_choice_wait_feedback: Waiting is free until the coach fills. Then it is the whole trip, not the forty.
card_trip_deposit_choice_wait_reaction: You wait. The coach fills seat by seat, and nobody calls.
card_trip_balance_due_situation: The school trip’s balance is due this month. Forty more, or the place goes back to the list.
card_trip_balance_due_choice_pay_feedbac: Forty now, and the trip is paid in full. The deposit held the place; this is what the place costs.
card_trip_balance_due_choice_pay_reactio: The transfer clears and the seat has your name on it.
card_trip_balance_due_choice_lose_feedba: The deposit stays with the company and the place goes to the next name. Twenty bought a hold on a trip you did not take.
card_trip_balance_due_choice_lose_reacti: You come off the list. The twenty does not come back.
card_hype_trainers_situation: The trainers everyone wants drop in four months at ◈90. Yours have a hole and still work.
card_hype_trainers_choice_save_label: Keep the money for the drop
card_hype_trainers_choice_save_feedback: The money stays in the envelope, and the drop has a date now. The date is the commitment.
card_hype_trainers_choice_save_reaction: The drop goes in the calendar: four months out.
card_hype_trainers_choice_later_feedback: When the drop lands, ninety will feel like news and the month will have to carry it. The version of you with money set aside is the version who gets them.
card_hype_trainers_choice_later_reaction: The trainers drop on a Tuesday. The group chat fills with photographs.
card_the_drop_situation: The trainers drop today at ◈90, and the group chat is already deciding. Yours still have a hole.
card_the_drop_choice_buy_feedback: Ninety, paid out of the money that was waiting for this. The trainers arrive, and the envelope goes quiet.
card_the_drop_choice_buy_reaction: Ninety leaves, and the trainers are on your feet.
card_the_drop_choice_let_go_feedback: The date was the commitment, not the purchase. The money stays in the envelope and the old pair does one more winter.
card_the_drop_choice_let_go_reaction: Drop day passes. The group chat fills with photographs.
card_pocket_money_gone_situation: The ◈40 landed a week ago. There is ◈12 left and you honestly cannot say where the rest went.
card_pocket_money_gone_choice_track_feed: The leak was a dozen small things you would have sworn were nothing. None of them looked like a leak while it was happening.
card_pocket_money_gone_choice_track_reac: One hour with a pen and the week is on paper.
card_pocket_money_gone_choice_shrug_feed: Twelve this week, twenty-eight that vanished. Weeks are how months are made, and this one went somewhere you cannot name.
card_pocket_money_gone_choice_shrug_reac: It is only twelve, so nothing is written down.
card_fixer_bike_situation: Thirty for the bike with the loose wheel, an hour to fit the one you already have. Or ◈40 for the one that works outside the shop.
card_fixer_bike_choice_fix_feedback: Thirty and an hour of your evening, and it rides. Time and money come from the same wallet; this time the cheaper half was time.
card_fixer_bike_choice_fix_reaction: An hour with a spanner, and the bike rides straight.
card_fixer_bike_choice_ready_feedback: Ten more than the fix, for a bike that asked nothing of you. That ten was the price of not getting your hands dirty.
card_fixer_bike_choice_ready_reaction: Forty, and the bike is ready at the shop door.
card_phone_plan_situation: Your parents will keep paying for the phone, but only if you take the ◈15 a month plan yourself. It comes out either way.
card_phone_plan_choice_take_feedback: Before you have earned anything, a cost arrives that does not care how the month went. Decide where it goes before the month decides for you.
card_phone_plan_choice_take_reaction: The plan is yours. Fifteen a month, whether the month was good or not.
card_phone_plan_choice_cheaper_label: Shop around for a cheaper one
card_phone_plan_choice_cheaper_feedback: Three hours of comparing, and a few units a month come back for as long as you keep it. Decide where it goes before the month decides for you.
card_phone_plan_choice_cheaper_reaction: Three hours of comparing, and the bill drops a few units a month.
card_first_budget_situation: Last month you planned carefully and still ended up ◈12 short. Nothing dramatic happened — it was a lot of small things.
card_first_budget_choice_cover_label: Cover it from what you saved
card_first_budget_choice_cover_feedback: Twelve out of the buffer, and the rest of the month went as planned. Small repairs are what the buffer quietly holds.
card_first_budget_choice_cover_reaction: Twelve comes out of the Save envelope, and the month squares up.
card_first_budget_choice_tighten_label: Spend an evening working out where it went
card_first_budget_choice_tighten_feedbac: Two hours to find twelve is a bad rate. It also found the six other small things quietly doing the same.
card_first_budget_choice_tighten_reactio: An evening with the statements, and the twelve is found.
card_savings_goal_situation: A ◈300 bike you actually want, or a number with nothing attached to it. Both are saving.
card_savings_goal_choice_bike_feedback: Now the envelope has a face on it. Give the money a name and it survives.
card_savings_goal_choice_bike_reaction: A picture of the bike goes on the Save envelope.
card_savings_goal_choice_number_label: Keep it in your pocket for now
card_savings_goal_choice_number_feedback: It stays a number for now, and numbers are easy to spend. Give the money a name and it survives.
card_savings_goal_choice_number_reaction: It stays a number, without a picture or a date.
card_subscription_creep_situation: You add it up for the first time: streaming, storage, a game pass, two apps you forgot about. ◈28 a month.
card_subscription_creep_choice_cut_label: Cancel the ones you forgot about
card_subscription_creep_choice_cut_feedb: Fourteen a month is small enough to never notice and permanent enough to matter.
card_subscription_creep_choice_cut_react: Ten minutes on the phone, and fourteen a month stops leaving.
card_subscription_creep_choice_keep_feed: They are small, and that is the whole trick: ◈28 a month is ◈336 a year, and it never shows up as one decision.
card_subscription_creep_choice_keep_reac: They stay. Twenty-eight a month, leaving in six small pieces.
card_concert_tickets_situation: Your friends are going tonight. Tickets are ◈35 and you have ◈60 saved toward the bike.
card_concert_tickets_choice_go_feedback: Spending from Save is allowed: the cascade decides how, and you decide whether. This month you decided yes.
card_concert_tickets_choice_go_reaction: Good night. The bike waits a little longer.
card_concert_tickets_choice_stay_feedbac: The thirty-five stayed in the bike fund. The night happened without you, and there is no refund for that.
card_concert_tickets_choice_stay_reactio: You stay in. The group chat is loud without you for one night.
card_phone_bill_spike_situation: The first bill arrives at ◈40. The plan said ◈15. The difference is data you apparently used without noticing.
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_pay_label: Pay it and watch the usage
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_pay_feedbac: Twenty-five for finding out that the plan and the bill are separate documents. Watching the usage is part of the month now.
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_pay_reactio: The bill takes forty. The plan said fifteen.
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_challenge_f: The charge was halved in twenty minutes. That is a real hourly rate, and the phone company counts on nobody calling.
card_phone_bill_spike_choice_challenge_r: Twenty minutes of hold music, and the charge comes back halved.
card_no_spend_week_situation: A zero-spend week: nothing that is not transport or food. Your friends think it is a joke.
card_no_spend_week_choice_do_feedback: Two hours of planning and a week that went where you said it would. The plan held for seven days, and you watched it hold.
card_no_spend_week_choice_do_reaction: Seven days of no, and the week goes where you said it would.
card_no_spend_week_choice_skip_feedback: Fifteen on the usual things. Nothing dramatic, which is exactly how an envelope empties.
card_no_spend_week_choice_skip_reaction: The week happens normally, and the usual small things happen with it.
card_gift_fund_situation: Three birthdays this month and presents will run about ◈30. Payday is not soon.
card_gift_fund_choice_plan_feedback: A list, a cap, and presents nobody squinted at. The same three birthdays, half the price.
card_gift_fund_choice_plan_reaction: The list goes on the fridge: three names, one cap.
card_gift_fund_choice_wing_feedback: Thirty, and two of the presents were panic decisions at the till. The queue did the choosing.
card_gift_fund_choice_wing_reaction: Two presents get chosen at the till, in a hurry, with a queue behind you.
card_savings_milestone_situation: The savings account says ◈200 for the first time. Nothing happened except you not spending it, sixteen times.
card_savings_milestone_choice_add_feedba: Two hundred, and the month’s saving stays where the plan put it. No single month made the two hundred; a lot of small decisions did.
card_savings_milestone_choice_add_reacti: The envelope stays sealed and the number keeps its shape.
card_savings_milestone_choice_celebrate_: Ten spent on the milestone, one hundred and ninety still working. The ten did the celebrating; the rest kept working.
Ten comes out, and something small and good happens.
card_data_plan_shrink_situation: The plan is ◈15 a month for more data than you have ever used. The smaller one is ◈9 and you will feel it on trips.
card_data_plan_shrink_choice_shrink_feed: Six a month back for ten minutes of admin. The smaller plan stings twice a year and pays every month.
card_data_plan_shrink_choice_shrink_reac: Ten minutes in the app, and the plan drops to nine.
card_data_plan_shrink_choice_stay_feedba: Comfort costs six a month. That is the trade: a little convenience now, a larger number by the end of school.
card_data_plan_shrink_choice_stay_reacti: The plan stays. The data stays unused, most of the time.
card_till_impulse_situation: Every shop puts the same small things by the till. You have walked past them four times this week and bought them twice.
card_till_impulse_choice_rule_feedback: One hour to set the rule, and the till aisle has a number on it now. The rule can hold on the days you are tired.
card_till_impulse_choice_rule_reaction: One hour decides what the till aisle is allowed to cost.
card_till_impulse_choice_buy_feedback: Twelve this week. The till aisle is not an accident; it is the most profitable square metre in the shop.
card_till_impulse_choice_buy_reaction: Twelve this week, and the snacks keep their spot by the till.
card_first_payslip_situation: The café takes you on, ten an hour. Your first shift is Saturday. Nobody has explained how many you will want.
card_first_payslip_choice_enthusiastic_f: Eighty for the month, and every weekend gone with it. The rota had your name on it, and the money followed the hours.
card_first_payslip_choice_enthusiastic_r: Every shift on the rota, and the first payslip is eighty.
card_first_payslip_choice_measured_feedb: Fifty for the month, and the week still has room in it. Two shifts a week is the price of an hour you can live with.
card_first_payslip_choice_measured_react: Two shifts a week, and fifty that keep coming.
card_interest_first_situation: Your savings went up this month and you did not put anything in. It was ◈0.12, and it was not there before.
card_interest_first_choice_more_feedback: The interest lands at the close without any hours from you. Interest is the only money that works while you sleep.
card_interest_first_choice_more_reaction: An hour of admin, and the plan carries twenty across at the close.
card_interest_first_choice_nothing_label: Leave it — twelve units is nothing
card_interest_first_choice_nothing_feedb: Twelve units this month, and the statement keeps its shape. Interest is the only money that works while you sleep.
card_interest_first_choice_nothing_react: The twelve units stay where they are and keep to themselves.
card_extra_shift_situation: Your manager is short-staffed on Saturday and asks if you can cover. It is the same day as the match.
card_extra_shift_choice_take_feedback: Eight hours at ten an hour, and it landed as eighty. The match happened without you; the eighty did not exist before the shift.
card_extra_shift_choice_take_reaction: Saturday disappears into the café, and eighty comes back.
card_extra_shift_choice_pass_feedback: Nothing wrong with that, and the eighty does not exist. Next month’s plan has to live without it.
card_extra_shift_choice_pass_reaction: You keep your Saturday. The rota finds somebody else.
card_bnpl_trainers_situation: The trainers are ◈120. The shop offers four monthly payments of ◈30, interest-free.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_now_feedback: Paid in one go, and nothing follows you into next month. The trainers cost what the ticket said.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_now_reaction: One hundred and twenty, paid, and the trainers leave with you.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_bnpl_feedback: Four payments of thirty, and the shop never asked about your file. Paying this perfectly builds nothing on it.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_bnpl_reaction: Four payments of thirty, starting now and ending in the spring.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_skip_feedback: Not this month, and nothing was lost by waiting. The trainers will still be trainers in the spring.
card_bnpl_trainers_choice_skip_reaction: The trainers stay in the window, and the month keeps its shape.
card_lend_to_friend_situation: Your mate needs ◈40 until next week. You have it. You have also watched them not pay people back.
card_lend_to_friend_choice_lend_feedback: Forty out of the Save envelope and a promise for next week. The money is theirs for now, and the question is theirs to answer.
card_lend_to_friend_choice_lend_reaction: Forty leaves the envelope, and your mate has it until next week.
card_lend_to_friend_choice_no_feedback: You kept the money and the awkwardness, and the week carried on. Saying no cost nothing except the sentence.
card_lend_to_friend_choice_no_reaction: The forty stays where it is, and the evening gets a little colder.
card_lend_returns_situation: Three weeks later your mate slides ◈20 across the table. The other twenty is definitely next week, and the group chat is already planning the next night out.
card_lend_returns_choice_take_feedback: Half came back without a conversation, and the rest is a question now. The friendship has a number in it.
card_lend_returns_choice_take_reaction: Twenty slides across the table, and the other twenty waits.
card_lend_returns_choice_chase_feedback: Forty recovered, and two hours of holding a friend at arm’s length. The money is square; the borrowing may not come your way again.
card_lend_returns_choice_chase_reaction: The full forty comes back, and the table goes quiet for a moment.
card_evening_course_situation: The college runs an evening coding course — three months, two evenings a week, ◈90 up front. Past students say the certificate is the part that gets you looked at.
card_evening_course_choice_enrol_feedbac: Ninety up front and two evenings a week. The certificate is the part that gets you looked at, and the evenings are what it costs.
card_evening_course_choice_enrol_reactio: Ninety up front, and two evenings a week until spring.
card_evening_course_choice_skip_feedback: Nothing changed this spring, and the evenings stayed yours. The certificate stayed in the photograph on the board.
card_evening_course_choice_skip_reaction: The noticeboard keeps the enrolment form, and the evenings stay free.
card_course_pays_off_situation: Last class done. The certificate sits in a drawer for a week, and then Priya offers you the closing shift — the one that pays a little more if you can hold the till and the book.
card_course_pays_off_choice_ask_feedback: Sixty more for the shifts nobody else wanted to ask about. The certificate opened the door and the ask walked through it.
card_course_pays_off_choice_ask_reaction: The number said out loud, and the better shifts are yours.
card_course_pays_off_choice_quiet_feedba: Thirty, and no conversation. The other thirty stayed in somebody else’s budget.
card_course_pays_off_choice_quiet_reacti: The shifts start, and the rate is the one on the board.
card_overtime_offer_situation: Ravi is ill and the café needs Friday and Saturday covered. It is ◈45 and your entire weekend.
card_overtime_offer_choice_take_feedback: The shifts were covered and the month is forty-five heavier. The weekend is the part the payslip does not show.
card_overtime_offer_choice_take_reaction: Ravi’s weekend goes to you, and forty-five comes with it.
card_overtime_offer_choice_pass_feedback: The café found another pair of hands and the weekend stayed whole. Forty-five never arrived; neither did the tired Monday.
card_overtime_offer_choice_pass_reaction: The Friday and Saturday stay unsold, and somebody else covers them.
card_inflated_prices_situation: The meal deal went up again. Same sandwich, ten per cent more, and it is the fourth thing this year that quietly did.
card_inflated_prices_choice_replan_feedb: The lines moved because the prices did, and the month balances again. Nothing else about the sandwich changed.
card_inflated_prices_choice_replan_react: Two hours with the numbers, and the envelopes move with the prices.
card_inflated_prices_choice_carry_feedba: Twelve more for the same lunch, absorbed without a rewrite. The sandwich did not shrink; only the month did.
card_inflated_prices_choice_carry_reacti: Twelve more this month, and the envelopes stay where they were written.
card_payday_timing_situation: The wage hits the account on Friday. By Sunday the weekend has taken a third of it, and the month is still twenty-eight days long.
card_payday_timing_choice_move_feedback: The month’s share moved aside on Friday, and the weekend spends what is left. Same wage, and a month with a floor under it.
card_payday_timing_choice_move_reaction: One hour on Friday, and the weekend gets a number.
card_payday_timing_choice_weekend_feedba: Twenty-five went on the weekend, and the rest of the month does the adjusting. The wage arrives once; the weekends keep arriving.
card_payday_timing_choice_weekend_reacti: Friday landed, Sunday took its cut, and the month keeps counting.
card_shift_clash_situation: The café offers you every Saturday for the next two months. Your friends have started planning things that happen on Saturdays.
card_shift_clash_choice_work_feedback: Sixty for eight Saturdays, and the plans happen without you. The money shows on the payslip; the other cost does not.
card_shift_clash_choice_work_reaction: Every Saturday for two months, and sixty lands on the payslip.
card_shift_clash_choice_life_feedback: Fifteen for the two weekends, and the plans still have you in them. The café filled the other Saturdays without much trouble.
card_shift_clash_choice_life_reaction: Two Saturdays stay free, and the plans get a familiar face.
card_meal_deal_situation: The meal deal is six: sandwich, drink, snack. The sandwich alone is four. The drink is one you would not have bought.
card_meal_deal_choice_alone_feedback: Four for the thing you came in for, and the drink stayed on the shelf. Lunch was the sandwich, so the sandwich is what got paid for.
card_meal_deal_choice_alone_reaction: The sandwich alone, four, and the queue moves on.
card_meal_deal_choice_deal_feedback: Six, and a snack you would not have bought on its own. The extra two units bought two things you did not come in for.
card_meal_deal_choice_deal_reaction: Six for all three, and the drink that was not on the list.
card_phone_repair_situation: The phone is cracked again. Repair is sixty; a refurbished one is a hundred and fifty, and yours has two good years left.
card_phone_repair_choice_repair_feedback: Sixty to keep the phone that knows your life. The refurbished one stays in the window, and yours keeps working.
card_phone_repair_choice_repair_reaction: Sixty to the repair shop, and the phone goes another year.
card_phone_repair_choice_replace_feedbac: One hundred and fifty for new glass and a fresh battery. The old phone still worked; that was the part nobody checked.
card_phone_repair_choice_replace_reactio: A hundred and fifty, and the old phone goes in the drawer.
card_cut_a_shift_situation: You are on the rota five evenings a week and the schoolwork is starting to show it. A shift is worth about thirty.
card_cut_a_shift_choice_cut_feedback: Thirty given up for the evenings, and the rota closes at three. The schoolwork noticed before you did.
card_cut_a_shift_choice_cut_reaction: Three evenings go back on the calendar, and thirty stops arriving.
card_cut_a_shift_choice_keep_feedback: Thirty for eight more hours, and the evenings shortened accordingly. The schoolwork is the line nobody printed.
card_cut_a_shift_choice_keep_reaction: All five evenings stay, and thirty comes with the extra hours.
card_trial_renewal_situation: The app you signed up to in the summer is about to bill you nine a month. You have opened it twice since June.
card_trial_renewal_choice_cancel_feedbac: Ten minutes before the renewal, and nine a month stayed yours. The app you opened twice is gone before it cost anything.
card_trial_renewal_choice_cancel_reactio: The trial ends without a bill, and the app closes quietly.
card_trial_renewal_choice_renew_feedback: Nine for something opened twice since June. The bill arrived on time, which is more than the app did.
card_trial_renewal_choice_renew_reaction: Nine leaves, and the app stays installed for another year.
card_quarterly_interest_situation: The statement has a new line: interest paid. Nine units have appeared that nobody worked for.
card_quarterly_interest_line_1: Interest paid this quarter: nine units.
card_quarterly_interest_choice_leave_fee: The nine stayed in the account, and the next statement adds to it. Small growth, and nothing to do about it.
card_quarterly_interest_choice_leave_rea: The nine stays in, and the line keeps growing on paper.
card_quarterly_interest_choice_skim_feed: Nine withdrawn, and the account is where it was before the interest landed. The line starts growing again from a smaller number.
card_quarterly_interest_choice_skim_reac: Nine out, and the account goes back to where it started.
card_bnpl_offer_situation: At seventeen the shop app now offers you a limit of ◈300. No card, no paperwork, no explanation of what happens if you do not pay.
card_bnpl_offer_choice_use_feedback: One tap, and three hundred was available. The limit is on the app now, above everything you look at.
card_bnpl_offer_choice_use_reaction: The limit goes through in one tap, and the basket is bigger.
card_bnpl_offer_choice_leave_feedback: You left the three hundred where it was. Next month it will be there, and the thing you nearly bought will not matter.
card_bnpl_offer_choice_leave_reaction: The limit stays untouched, and the home screen looks the same.
card_minimum_payment_situation: Your card statement arrives. You owe ◈300. The minimum payment is ◈15, and the full payment is — well, ◈300.
card_minimum_payment_choice_full_feedbac: Three hundred in one go, and the balance is gone before interest finds it. The minimum is designed to be affordable forever; you paid past it.
card_minimum_payment_choice_full_reactio: Three hundred, paid, and the statement closes clean.
card_minimum_payment_choice_minimum_feed: Fifteen today, and the rest of the balance follows you for six months. The minimum is designed to be affordable forever.
card_minimum_payment_choice_minimum_reac: Fifteen now, and forty-seven fifty every month after.
card_credit_limit_rise_situation: Your limit goes from ◈300 to ◈800. Nothing about your income changed. A friend points out you could finally afford the trip.
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_accept_lab: Put the trip on the card
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_accept_fee: The trip was real and so is the balance behind it. Three hundred became eight hundred, and none of it was income.
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_accept_rea: The trip goes on the card, and the limit has room.
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_ignore_fee: The limit was never your money. It is the bank’s number, not your raise.
card_credit_limit_rise_choice_ignore_rea: The trip waits for the savings, and the limit sits unused.
card_overdraft_situation: Five days until you are paid and you are ◈40 short. Three friends are going out tonight.
card_overdraft_choice_dip_feedback: The bank charged for the favour and the file noticed. Forty borrowed at a rate nobody agreed to.
card_overdraft_choice_dip_reaction: The account goes negative, and the bank covers it for a fee.
card_overdraft_choice_wait_feedback: Five days out and the file unchanged. The free version of the same week cost a few evenings.
card_overdraft_choice_wait_reaction: Five days in, and the account holds its line.
card_rent_share_situation: Friends want you in a shared flat. Your share is ◈650, plus a deposit, plus the things nobody lists when they quote a rent.
card_rent_share_choice_commit_feedback: Six hundred and fifty a month, and the deposit before that. Every other line in the month has to fit around it now.
card_rent_share_choice_commit_reaction: The deposit goes through, and there is an address with your name on it.
card_rent_share_choice_wait_feedback: You stayed put, and the deposit stayed saved. It cost nothing and it bought time.
card_rent_share_choice_wait_reaction: The flat fills with other names, and your room stays where it was.
card_late_fee_situation: The payment came out on a day the account was empty. The bank wants ◈25 for the privilege.
card_late_fee_choice_pay_feedback: The fee is behind you, and next month’s payment starts from a clean line. Twenty-five bought the month back.
card_late_fee_choice_pay_reaction: Twenty-five to the bank, and the account is level again.
card_late_fee_choice_leave_feedback: It sits there, unpaid, and the record keeps it longer than the month will. The fee was the cheap part.
card_late_fee_choice_leave_reaction: The fee stays on the account and starts writing itself down.
card_instalment_week_situation: The payment goes out this week and the week is already thin. You said the same thing last month.
card_instalment_week_choice_tighten_feed: Two hours of cooking instead of a week of buying. The payment was decided months ago; the week was decided today.
card_instalment_week_choice_tighten_reac: A week of cooking, and the payment goes out on time.
card_instalment_week_choice_dip_feedback: Thirty out of savings to feed a month-old decision. The four payments took their next bite.
card_instalment_week_choice_dip_reaction: Thirty out of savings, and the week goes back to normal.
card_score_check_situation: The banking app has a number for you now: 640. It went down five points and nothing on screen says why.
card_score_check_choice_read_feedback: Five points down, and a page that says which payments move the number. The explanation costs two hours and nothing else.
card_score_check_choice_read_reaction: The page opens, and the rules are written down.
card_score_check_choice_close_feedback: The number is still there and still moving, deciding what the next loan costs. Not looking changes nothing about either.
card_score_check_choice_close_reaction: The app closes, and the number stays on its server.
card_score_goal_situation: The phone contract needs a credit check. No score means a deposit of a hundred, or buying a handset outright today.
card_score_goal_choice_wait_feedback: Two hours to see which payments move the number. The deposit exists because nobody can look at you yet.
card_score_goal_choice_wait_reaction: The check waits, and the deposit stays hypothetical.
card_score_goal_choice_outright_feedback: One hundred and twenty to skip a queue nobody wanted to be in. The phone is yours and nothing about it is owed.
card_score_goal_choice_outright_reaction: One hundred and twenty on the counter, and the handset is yours.
card_refuse_the_limit_situation: The shop app now lets you spread four hundred in four payments. It suggests this at the checkout now, above the button.
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_stick_label: Stick to what you can repay
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_stick_feedb: The basket went down to what the account could cover. The button was doing arithmetic you never saw.
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_stick_react: The basket comes down, and the one-tap button goes unused.
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_basket_feed: Eighty over four payments, decided in a second. The button was placed above the one that said no.
card_refuse_the_limit_choice_basket_reac: Eighty spread over four payments, and the checkout is pleased.
card_credit_check_free_situation: The bank lets you see your score for free, with a page explaining every line. It takes about an evening.
card_credit_check_free_choice_read_feedb: Two hours to find the late payment and the fix. The report has been sitting there for free the whole time.
card_credit_check_free_choice_read_react: An evening with the report, and one line needs a phone call.
card_credit_check_free_choice_skip_feedb: Skipped, and the number moved anyway. The people who watch it pay less for the same borrowing.
card_credit_check_free_choice_skip_react: The report stays unread, and the number keeps moving.
card_bnpl_pressure_situation: The group is buying the same trainers in four payments. Nobody is talking about what the third payment feels like in a thin month.
card_bnpl_pressure_choice_save_feedback: The money stayed in the envelope and the trainers waited until it existed. No third payment can find a thin month now.
card_bnpl_pressure_choice_save_reaction: Two months of waiting, and the trainers are not here yet.
card_bnpl_pressure_choice_split_feedback: Four payments, and the first is not the problem. The third lands in the month you cannot see yet.
card_bnpl_pressure_choice_split_reaction: Four payments start, and the first one is easy.
card_payday_drain_situation: The wage landed Friday and the account is already thin. Nothing big happened; a lot of small things did.
card_payday_drain_choice_map_feedback: The same Friday has come twice a month for a year; this is the first time it is on paper. The month explains itself once the drips are written down.
card_payday_drain_choice_map_reaction: Three hours with the month, and the Friday is on a line.
card_payday_drain_choice_wait_feedback: Twenty that went somewhere unplanned, and none of it was memorable. The month emptied without a single decision.
card_payday_drain_choice_wait_reaction: The month settles on its own, and twenty finds somewhere to go.
card_the_fork_situation: That is it — school done. Study, or start working? This one you do not get back.
card_the_fork_choice_study_label: Study — part-time work, and a 3,000 loan
card_the_fork_choice_study_feedback: Three thousand borrowed against the years ahead, and the first term has a date. The number on the sheet is real from today.
card_the_fork_choice_study_reaction: The loan is signed, and the first term has a start date.
card_the_fork_choice_work_label: Work — full time, and a flat of your own
card_the_fork_choice_work_feedback: Rent leaves before the first wage lands, and the deposit came out of the years when the money had nowhere to go. The keys are the first thing the saving bought.
card_the_fork_choice_work_reaction: Full time from Monday, and the deposit on the flat is paid.
card_first_taxed_payslip_situation: Your first full payslip shows a number you agreed to and a smaller number arriving. Between them sits a line called withholding.
card_first_taxed_payslip_line_1: Hours: every hour you agreed to.
card_first_taxed_payslip_line_2: Withholding: the line between the two numbers.
card_first_taxed_payslip_choice_read_fee: A fifth left before the money arrived, and the line between the two numbers has a name. It is the deduction you never have to sit down and pay.
card_first_taxed_payslip_choice_read_rea: The payslip is read line by line, and the two numbers make sense.
card_first_taxed_payslip_choice_ignore_f: The deduction happened without being read, the way it happens every month. Two minutes would have explained it.
card_first_taxed_payslip_choice_ignore_r: The number is taken, and the payslip goes in the folder.
card_the_fund_situation: Your savings keep pace with rising prices and barely beat them. There is a fund that has averaged seven per cent a year, and lost a quarter in a bad one.
card_the_fund_choice_open_feedback: Four hundred into something that moves. The price of the moving is that it can move down first.
card_the_fund_choice_open_reaction: The Fund takes the four hundred and starts drawing a line.
card_the_fund_choice_wait_feedback: You stayed in savings: steady, available, and a hair behind the prices. Neither answer was wrong this month.
card_the_fund_choice_wait_reaction: The savings stay where they are, and the Fund keeps its distance.
card_the_crash_situation: Everything in the fund is down a quarter in two months. Everyone on the internet has an opinion and all of them are panicking.
card_the_crash_choice_buy_label: Put more in while it is cheap
card_the_crash_choice_buy_feedback: You added while everyone was selling, and nobody knows where the bottom is. You cannot time it. You can only stay in it.
card_the_crash_choice_buy_reaction: More goes in while the market is down, and the screen stays red.
card_the_crash_choice_hold_feedback: You held while the quarter disappeared from the screen. Nothing was sold, so nothing was locked. You cannot time it. You can only stay in it.
card_the_crash_choice_hold_reaction: The Fund stays as it is, and the fall lands on paper only.
card_the_crash_choice_sell_feedback: You sold at the bottom and locked the fall in. The story felt most convincing right there. You cannot time it. You can only stay in it.
card_the_crash_choice_sell_reaction: The Fund is sold at the fallen price, and the money goes to savings.
card_scam_opportunity_situation: A message from someone who knows a friend of yours. ◈200 becomes ◈600 in six weeks, guaranteed, but you have to move today.
card_scam_opportunity_line_1: My brother has done this three times. Send ◈200 today and you are in before the round closes.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_in_feedback: Guaranteed, urgent, and paid by transfer — three words that never sit together. Urgency is the tell. The two hundred is gone.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_in_reaction: Two hundred leaves by transfer, and the round closes.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_check_feedb: You asked why today, and no answer came. Urgency is the tell, and the page had nothing else behind it.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_check_react: The message gets a question, and the countdown runs out.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_block_feedb: Gone, and the same story will come back with a different name. Urgency is the tell.
card_scam_opportunity_choice_block_react: The message is deleted, and the number is blocked.
card_app_tip_situation: Danny has an app. His cousin turned ◈40 into ◈52 last month and has screenshots. The button says invest and the countdown says nine minutes.
card_app_tip_line_1: Danny: Cousin sent the screenshots. I put in ◈40 on Tuesday.
card_app_tip_choice_in_feedback: An app with a cartoon rocket, a countdown, and a cousin’s screenshots. The button said invest, and the clock said nine minutes.
card_app_tip_choice_in_reaction: Fifty goes in, and the app shows a rocket and a countdown.
card_app_tip_choice_out_label: Ask where the returns come from
card_app_tip_choice_out_feedback: He did not know where the returns came from, and nobody else asked. The chat found a different subject by evening.
card_app_tip_choice_out_reaction: The question is asked, and the group chat moves on.
card_app_vanishes_situation: The app is gone from the store. Danny’s cousin is typing in capitals. Yesterday your ◈50 showed as ◈68, and today there is no screen at all.
card_app_vanishes_line_1: Danny: I keep refreshing the store. Cousin says it is coming back tonight.
card_app_vanishes_choice_report_feedback: The money left by choice and cannot be clawed back. The two hours still put a name on a list, and the list catches somebody eventually.
card_app_vanishes_choice_report_reaction: The fraud line is called, and two hours go into a report.
card_app_vanishes_choice_chalk_feedback: Fifty lost to a story with screenshots. The version of this mistake that costs two hundred never happened.
card_app_vanishes_choice_chalk_reaction: Fifty stays lost, and the app stays gone.
card_the_limit_letter_situation: The card company has raised your limit to ◈500 and would like you to know it is there for you.
card_the_limit_letter_choice_ignore_feed: None of the five hundred was used, and the balance kept its shape. The letter had offered; the drawer was the answer.
card_the_limit_letter_choice_ignore_reac: The letter goes in the drawer, and the five hundred stays where it is.
card_the_limit_letter_choice_use_feedbac: Sixty decided now and repaid later, and the ceiling moves closer by sixty. The letter got its wish.
card_the_limit_letter_choice_use_reactio: Sixty goes on the card, and the headroom gets smaller.
card_cash_in_hand_situation: A builder pays you ◈120 in notes for clearing a site. Nothing is written down anywhere.
card_cash_in_hand_choice_declare_feedbac: The work went through the books and the month kept ninety. There is a version of the afternoon that exists on paper, and this is it.
card_cash_in_hand_choice_declare_reactio: Ninety stays after the deduction, and the work is on the record.
card_cash_in_hand_choice_quiet_feedback: One hundred and twenty, untouched and unrecorded. Nothing happens until something else does, and then there is no history of the work at all.
card_cash_in_hand_choice_quiet_reaction: One hundred and twenty stays in notes, and nothing is written down.
card_refund_text_situation: A text says the tax office owes you ◈240. The link asks for your bank details, and the deadline is today.
card_refund_text_line_1: You have ◈240 waiting. Confirm the bank details before the file closes today.
card_refund_text_choice_click_feedback: A refund never claimed, a link, and a deadline. The two hundred forty was the hook; the one hundred twenty was the price.
card_refund_text_choice_click_reaction: The details go in, and the tax office is not the one receiving.
card_refund_text_choice_check_feedback: One hour on the tax site and the message was obviously a message. Refunds arrive in writing, from numbers nobody had to chase.
card_refund_text_choice_check_reaction: The real site is opened, and the text looks different by then.
card_boring_fund_situation: A friend of a friend turned ◈300 into ◈2,000 in a month. He is posting the screenshots again.
card_boring_fund_choice_fund_label: Put it in the boring fund
card_boring_fund_choice_fund_feedback: Fifty at seven per cent, on a graph that moves too slowly to post. The slow part is the offer.
card_boring_fund_choice_fund_reaction: Fifty goes into the boring fund, and the graph crawls.
card_boring_fund_choice_chase_label: Put thirty in the same thing
card_boring_fund_choice_chase_feedback: Thirty in after the story, which is when the story is most expensive. The screenshots were of a rise that already happened.
card_boring_fund_choice_chase_reaction: Thirty goes in after the screenshot, and the peak was last month.
card_first_statement_situation: One page, two numbers that matter: the full balance, or the minimum that keeps everything going.
card_first_statement_choice_clear_feedba: Paid in full before the interest existed. No fee, no letter next month, and the number moves the right way.
card_first_statement_choice_clear_reacti: The balance is paid, and the page closes with nothing due.
card_first_statement_choice_minimum_feed: Ten now, and the rest of the balance waits on the page. The card is still open and the page will be back next month.
card_first_statement_choice_minimum_reac: Ten now, and the balance stays where it is.
card_payslip_error_situation: The payslip says sixty-two hours. You worked seventy. The difference is about ◈45 before the deduction line even sees it.
card_payslip_error_choice_query_feedback: Forty-five arrives with the next pay, after an evening of proving hours the rota had already recorded. The mistake was theirs; the chasing was yours.
card_payslip_error_choice_query_reaction: Three hours of rota printouts, and the hours arrive next pay.
card_payslip_error_choice_drop_feedback: Forty-five left on the table because chasing felt awkward. Nobody else will chase it either.
card_payslip_error_choice_drop_reaction: Forty-five stays on the table, and the awkwardness goes nowhere.
card_side_work_situation: A mate’s market stall needs a hand on weekends. Forty a day, cash, and both days are possible.
card_side_work_choice_take_feedback: The stall got both days, and the cash landed in notes. Sunday night is the part the notes do not show.
card_side_work_choice_take_reaction: Both days at the market, and eighty for the weekend.
card_side_work_choice_one_feedback: Forty and a Sunday left standing. Half the money, half the weekend, and next Saturday is still a possibility.
card_side_work_choice_one_reaction: One day at the stall, and forty comes home.
card_grown_up_cover_situation: You now own enough that losing it would matter. Cover on everything you own is ◈12 a month.
card_grown_up_cover_odds: Roughly 1 in 12 renters claim in a given year.
card_grown_up_cover_choice_insure_feedba: Twelve a month, and a claim would not empty the flat. The months it goes unused are the same twelve.
card_grown_up_cover_choice_insure_reacti: Twelve a month, and the flat’s contents are covered.
card_grown_up_cover_choice_risk_feedback: You kept the twelve and the odds came with you. Most years that is the right trade, and the other years are expensive.
card_grown_up_cover_choice_risk_reaction: The twelve stays in the month, and the flat stays as it is.
card_rent_due_situation: Rent leaves on the first. It is more than half of everything you bring in, and it does not care what the rest of the month looked like.
card_rent_due_choice_pay_label: Pay it and plan around it
card_rent_due_choice_pay_feedback: Paid first, everything else second. The biggest fixed number sets the month’s shape, and this month it was paid without a chase.
card_rent_due_choice_pay_reaction: Rent leaves first, and the rest of the month knows it.
card_rent_due_choice_delay_label: Let it go late this once
card_rent_due_choice_delay_feedback: Late once this time, and the fee is the smallest part of the bill. The next month starts with the same number and less room.
card_rent_due_choice_delay_reaction: The rent goes late, and the fee lands on top of it.
card_graduate_job_situation: Full-time, twelve and a half an hour, and the training nobody offers you in person. It is more than you have ever earned.
card_graduate_job_choice_take_feedback: The wage is the small part of this one. What the job lets you handle next is the part that stays.
card_graduate_job_choice_take_reaction: The offer is signed, and full-time starts on Monday.
card_graduate_job_choice_push_feedback: Two hours of preparation for a number that stays for years. The asking was the paid part.
card_graduate_job_choice_push_reaction: The number is asked for, and the contract comes back higher.
card_commute_costs_situation: The monthly travel pass is ◈90. Walking is an hour each way, and the shifts already finish late.
card_commute_costs_choice_pass_feedback: Ninety to arrive with a life left. The walk looked cheaper until the hours were priced.
card_commute_costs_choice_pass_reaction: Ninety for the pass, and the mornings stop being a march.
card_commute_costs_choice_walk_feedback: Twelve hours a month on your own feet, and the shifts finish late. The job pays the wage and charges the journey.
card_commute_costs_choice_walk_reaction: An hour each way, and ninety stays where it was.
card_shift_swap_situation: The late shift pays two an hour more and finishes after the last bus. Nobody else wants it.
card_shift_swap_choice_late_feedback: Sixty for the hours nobody else wanted. The last bus leaves before the shift does, and the extra two an hour is why.
card_shift_swap_choice_late_reaction: The late shift is taken, and two more an hour comes with it.
card_shift_swap_choice_early_feedback: You kept the evenings and left the premium on the table. The bus home still runs when the shift ends.
card_shift_swap_choice_early_reaction: The early shifts stay, and the premium goes to somebody else.
card_ask_for_rise_situation: You have covered eleven shifts in a row and the wage has not moved. The manager is in the office.
card_ask_for_rise_choice_ask_feedback: Two hours of preparation and forty that stays every month after. The rota did not change; the rate did.
card_ask_for_rise_choice_ask_reaction: The manager is asked, and the wage moves by forty.
card_ask_for_rise_choice_wait_feedback: Eleven shifts straight and the same rate on all of them. Being noticed is not on the rota.
card_ask_for_rise_choice_wait_reaction: The shifts keep coming, and the wage stays where it was.
card_housemate_leaves_situation: A flatmate is moving out. Until someone else signs, the rent is a hundred a month more than the plan.
card_housemate_leaves_choice_cover_feedb: A hundred out of what was set aside, and the flat was paid in full. The buffer took it and will notice the difference.
card_housemate_leaves_choice_cover_react: A hundred goes on the rent, and the flat stays yours.
card_housemate_leaves_choice_advertise_f: Six hours of viewings and awkward questions. The room will fill, and the gap shrinks when it does.
card_housemate_leaves_choice_advertise_r: The room goes up online, and the viewings start.
card_boots_situation: The site needs steel-toe boots. New is ◈70; a barely-used pair is ◈30 if you can find the size.
card_boots_choice_new_feedback: Seventy and the right size straight away. The boots get paid for by the job, and today the job was not paying.
card_boots_choice_new_reaction: Seventy for the right size, and the site has its boots.
card_boots_choice_used_feedback: Thirty and four hours of hunting for the same steel. The difference was paid in time, which the month had.
card_boots_choice_used_reaction: Thirty for a used pair, and an afternoon of looking.
card_student_budget_situation: The loan lands, and it feels like income. It is not income. It is next year’s money arriving early, with your name on it.
card_student_budget_choice_spread_label: Put the term’s rent aside now
card_student_budget_choice_spread_feedba: An hour with the calendar, and the rent is spoken for before the month can reach it. What is left has a job for every week.
card_student_budget_choice_spread_reacti: The term’s rent goes aside, and the loan stops looking like income.
card_student_budget_choice_celebrate_fee: The loan lands and the first month spends like a wage. The rent is still in the same account, waiting for a later month.
card_student_budget_choice_celebrate_rea: The loan lands, and the first month feels rich.
card_textbook_week_situation: Three books on the list, ◈120 new. Second-hand copies are about ◈15 each, if you can find them.
card_textbook_week_choice_hunt_feedback: Forty-five and an afternoon of messages. The pages are the same; the cover is older.
card_textbook_week_choice_hunt_reaction: Second-hand copies are found, and forty-five buys all three.
card_textbook_week_choice_new_feedback: One hundred and twenty for the convenience of starting today. The lecture is the same, and the receipt is not.
card_textbook_week_choice_new_reaction: Three new books, and the list is done today.
card_exam_crunch_situation: Exams in a fortnight and the café would give you every shift you asked for.
card_exam_crunch_choice_revise_feedback: Eight hours in the quiet room. The shifts will still be there in three weeks; the exam will not.
card_exam_crunch_choice_revise_reaction: The library week is booked, and the shifts wait.
card_exam_crunch_choice_shifts_feedback: Fifty for a fortnight you will not get back before the exam. The money is in the account; the revision is not.
card_exam_crunch_choice_shifts_reaction: The shifts are taken, and fifty arrives before the exam does.
card_internship_lead_situation: A lab wants a summer helper — real work, a reference at the end, and two days a week all summer.
card_internship_lead_choice_take_feedbac: A hundred for the summer, and a reference that lasts longer than the summer. The shifts not taken are what it cost.
card_internship_lead_choice_take_reactio: The placement is signed, and the summer fills with lab hours.
card_internship_lead_choice_focus_feedba: The summer went to the term, and the term went to you. Nothing was wasted, and the lab found somebody else.
card_internship_lead_choice_focus_reacti: The summer stays free, and the term gets all of it.
card_student_discount_situation: A railcard is ◈30 and takes a third off every train home for a year. You go home about once a month.
card_student_discount_choice_buy_feedbac: Thirty up front, and the trips home cost less from now on. The saving starts with the first journey.
card_student_discount_choice_buy_reactio: Thirty for the railcard, and every trip home gets cheaper.
card_student_discount_choice_fare_feedba: Fifteen this trip and fifteen next, at the counter each time. The card stayed in the wallet, and the trips cost more.
card_student_discount_choice_fare_reacti: Full fare today, and the choice stays open.
card_study_group_coffee_title: The group meets at a café
card_study_group_coffee_situation: The study group meets three times a week at a café, and everyone buys something. The cheapest thing is four.
card_study_group_coffee_choice_round_fee: Twenty-four a month for the table and the usual. It is a real cost, and it is on the sheet now.
card_study_group_coffee_choice_round_rea: The usual gets ordered, and the group keeps its table.
card_study_group_coffee_choice_host_feed: Three hours of tidying and a kettle, and the café lost its table. Belonging is still paid for; only the currency changed.
card_study_group_coffee_choice_host_reac: The group moves to yours, and the kettle goes on three times.
card_the_second_year_situation: School starts again and the allowance is the same. From this year there is a bill with your name on it, every month.
card_the_second_year_choice_begin_feedba: Fifteen. A fixed cost arrives before any money does, and this is the first month planned backwards from it.
card_the_second_year_choice_begin_reacti: The year turns. The timetable goes back on the fridge.
card_the_third_year_situation: School, year three. The café has your name on the rota now, and the money starts coming from the hours you give it.
card_the_third_year_choice_begin_feedbac: The allowance stops and the wages start. The hours you sell come out of the week you already had.
card_the_third_year_choice_begin_reactio: The year turns. The café rota goes up on the fridge.
card_the_fourth_year_situation: Seventeen. The shop apps have found you, and everything they offer arrives in one tap.
card_the_fourth_year_choice_begin_feedba: A limit is offered before the income that would pay it. That gap is what this year is made of.
card_the_fourth_year_choice_begin_reacti: The year turns. The apps find the phone in your pocket.
callback_first_spent: The first allowance went the same way.
callback_first_kept: The first allowance stayed where you put it.
callback_checked_the_message: The last message like this one wanted bank details.
callback_carrying_a_balance: One of those is still being paid off.
callback_the_minimum_file: The minimum is still on the file.
callback_sold_before: The last thing you cleared out sold.
callback_overdraft_taste: The last dip cost more than the shop said.
callback_lent_before: The waiting was the expensive part last time.
callback_asked_and_it_moved: You have asked before, and the answer moved.
callback_danny_still_talking: Danny’s screenshots are still in the chat.
card_mum_late_pay_situation: Mum’s pay is stuck in the system and the shop does not take notes. She asks you to cover the week and promises to square it when the money lands.
card_mum_late_pay_line_1: Mum: Can you get the shop this week? I’ll square it the moment it lands.
card_mum_late_pay_choice_cover_feedback: Twenty-five keeps the fridge full and the week normal. She says she will square it, and the promise is the whole payment plan.
card_mum_late_pay_choice_cover_reaction: The trolley goes through and the card works.
card_mum_late_pay_choice_wait_feedback: Nothing moves today. The shop will stretch and the last days of the week get thin — that is the cost of waiting, and it is a real one.
card_mum_late_pay_choice_wait_reaction: The list stays on the fridge and the cupboards get creative.
card_mum_pays_back_situation: Mum’s pay lands. The shop money comes back in an envelope, with a little more than you put in.
card_mum_pays_back_choice_take_feedback: Thirty lands a week after the fridge was empty. The extra is not interest — it is what she decided a favour was worth.
card_mum_pays_back_choice_take_reaction: The envelope comes back lighter by thirty.
card_mum_pays_back_choice_leave_feedback: The envelope stays on the table. Nothing is owed and nothing is banked, and next week’s shop happens the same way either way.
card_mum_pays_back_choice_leave_reaction: She puts it back on the dresser and says nothing more.
card_trip_everyone_pays_situation: The trip is booked and the group chat is moving fast. The deposit is thirty tonight, or your name comes off the list.
card_trip_everyone_pays_choice_deposit_f: Thirty holds the place. The rest falls due in a later month with plans of its own — the deposit is the cheapest part of going.
card_trip_everyone_pays_choice_deposit_r: Your name stays on the list and the chat moves on.
card_trip_everyone_pays_choice_later_fee: The list closes tonight. Thirty stays in the month, and the weekend goes to whoever says yes first.
card_trip_everyone_pays_choice_later_rea: The chat keeps moving without your name in it.
card_trip_final_call_situation: The trip’s balance is due and the group’s patience is not. Sixty now, or the place goes to the next name.
card_trip_final_call_choice_pay_feedback: Sixty finishes the trip. The month gets tight exactly where it was going to be easy, and the weekend stops being a question.
card_trip_final_call_choice_pay_reaction: The transfer clears and the trip is real.
card_trip_final_call_choice_sell_spot_fe: Someone wants the seat badly enough to pay twenty for it. The weekend goes back to the calendar, unbooked and unspent.
card_trip_final_call_choice_sell_spot_re: The seat changes hands and the chat moves to somebody else.
card_birthday_money_situation: A birthday card arrives with fifty folded inside and nobody to spend it on but you.
card_birthday_money_choice_bank_feedback: Fifty that no week planned for. It joins the saved money and disappears from the spending that was going to find a use for it.
card_birthday_money_choice_bank_reaction: The envelope goes in the drawer, emptied.
card_birthday_money_choice_treat_feedbac: Twenty buys the evening and the rest stays folded. The treat is small, the leftover is real, and the card did not say which to choose.
card_birthday_money_choice_treat_reactio: Twenty goes on the night and thirty stays folded.
card_laptop_cover_situation: The shop offers protection for the laptop, folded into the receipt like part of the price.
card_laptop_cover_odds: About 1 in 4 laptops this old needs a paid repair within two years.
card_laptop_cover_choice_add_cover_feedb: Eight now turns an undated repair into the shop’s problem. If the repair never comes, the eight bought a quieter two years.
card_laptop_cover_choice_add_cover_react: The cover joins the policy and the receipt gets longer.
card_laptop_cover_choice_run_it_feedback: Eight stays in the month. The odds are on the page, and the shop is happy either way.
card_laptop_cover_choice_run_it_reaction: The receipt closes and the cover is not on it.
card_mum_late_week_situation: Mum is on late shifts all week, so the tea is you or it is takeaway.
card_mum_late_week_choice_cook_feedback: Three hours in the kitchen and the money stays put. The hours come out of the same week as everything else.
card_mum_late_week_choice_cook_reaction: The oven goes on and the kitchen smells like a plan.
card_mum_late_week_choice_takeaway_feedb: Twelve ends the argument with the saucepan and the evening stays yours. The money is the part that does not come back.
card_mum_late_week_choice_takeaway_react: One phone call and the tea arrives in bags.
card_priya_shift_swap_situation: Priya needs Saturday covered at the café. She will take one of your shifts when you need it back.
card_priya_shift_swap_line_1: Priya: I’m short on Saturday. Cover me and I’ll take one of yours later.
card_priya_shift_swap_choice_take_feedba: Ten hours of the weekend for forty, and one favour owed to you. The shift is real money; the favour is a promise between two people.
card_priya_shift_swap_choice_take_reacti: Saturday goes to the café and forty comes back.
card_priya_shift_swap_choice_cant_feedba: The Saturday stays yours and Priya asks someone else. No hours, no money, nothing owed in either direction.
card_priya_shift_swap_choice_cant_reacti: She nods and sends the shift round the group instead.
card_priya_swap_back_situation: Priya has not forgotten the Saturday, and she offers to take your shift this week.
card_priya_swap_back_choice_call_it_in_f: She covers the shift and the day comes back to you — eight hours nothing else had claimed.
card_priya_swap_back_choice_call_it_in_r: Saturday stays yours and Priya clocks in instead.
card_priya_swap_back_choice_let_it_go_fe: Nothing moves this week. The favour stays where it is, waiting for a week that needs it more.
card_priya_swap_back_choice_let_it_go_re: She waits a beat, then asks someone else.
card_grandma_asks_help_situation: Grandma is moving to the smaller flat and the boxes will not move themselves. She asks for the weekend, or for a man with a van.
card_grandma_asks_help_choice_go_feedbac: Six hours of lifting and tea, no money either way. The flat gets moved; the weekend gets spent. Both of those are true.
card_grandma_asks_help_choice_go_reactio: The boxes ride the lift down and the kettle goes on twice.
card_grandma_asks_help_choice_send_money: Fifteen pays the man with the van and keeps the weekend. It does not pay for the afternoon you were not there for.
The van is booked and the boxes leave without you.
card_grandma_sends_thanks_situation: A card arrives in the post with forty inside and a line about the boxes.
card_grandma_sends_thanks_choice_take_fe: Forty, posted like the last one. She has decided what the weekend was worth and sent it; sending it back would cost her more than it costs you.
card_grandma_sends_thanks_choice_take_re: The card goes on the shelf and the forty goes in your pocket.
card_grandma_sends_thanks_choice_send_it: The envelope goes back with a note inside. Nothing is banked, and the weekend stays a favour rather than a job.
The envelope is back in the post the next morning.
card_cashback_error_situation: The bank refunds a fee twice, and thirty sits in your account by mistake.
card_cashback_error_choice_say_so_feedba: One call and the thirty leaves again. The account is honest and poorer, and nothing about the week changes either way.
card_cashback_error_choice_say_so_reacti: The call takes minutes and the refund is reversed.
card_cashback_error_choice_say_nothing_f: The thirty stays. Banks find their own mistakes eventually, and until then it is the bank’s arithmetic, not your problem.
card_cashback_error_choice_say_nothing_r: The balance holds the thirty and nothing else happens.
card_burst_pipe_situation: A pipe under the sink gives up on a Tuesday night, and the water finds the floor before anyone finds the stopcock.
card_burst_pipe_choice_call_now_feedback: The emergency rate is what it is: the water stops and the bill lands. Cover pays it, or the month does.
card_burst_pipe_choice_call_now_reaction: The van arrives, the pipe is capped, and the floor is mopped.
card_burst_pipe_choice_tape_it_feedback: Thirty of tape, a bucket, and a night on the floor. The cheap fix is real until it is not, and it is paid for in hours.
card_burst_pipe_choice_tape_it_reaction: The tape holds through the night and the bucket needs emptying.
card_ravi_needs_cover_situation: Ravi is off sick again and asks if you can take his weekend shifts. He says he will get you back.
card_ravi_needs_cover_line_1: Ravi: Still not right. Any chance you take the weekend for me?
card_ravi_needs_cover_choice_cover_feedb: Twelve hours of the weekend for fifty-five, and Ravi back on his feet without the shop chasing him. The hours are real, and so is the favour.
card_ravi_needs_cover_choice_cover_react: The weekend goes to the shop and Ravi stays home.
card_ravi_needs_cover_choice_cant_feedba: The weekend stays yours and the shop finds somebody. He says it is fine; the favour goes unspent.
card_ravi_needs_cover_choice_cant_reacti: He says not to worry, and the rota gets rewritten.
card_ravi_returns_favour_situation: Ravi is back, and the weekend he owes you has become a choice: his shift, or a lead on better hours.
card_ravi_returns_favour_choice_take_shi: Six hours for fifty, handed over without a word about who owes who. The favour closes clean.
He clocks off and you clock on.
card_ravi_returns_favour_choice_take_lea: Thirty and your name passed to the manager. Less money, better hours — the favour spent on a door instead of a shift.
A number is passed along and the rota gets a new name.
card_danny_flat_night_situation: Danny has the flat for the night and everyone is in. Forty-five each, food and the door covered, paid on the night.
card_danny_flat_night_line_1: Danny: Everyone’s in. Forty-five a head, pay on the night.
card_danny_flat_night_choice_chip_in_fee: Forty-five, on the night, with the month’s wants already spoken for. The evening costs what it costs, and the envelope finds out afterwards.
card_danny_flat_night_choice_chip_in_rea: The money goes over and the night starts.
card_danny_flat_night_choice_stay_in_fee: The night goes on without you. Forty-five stays in the month, and the chat has the pictures by morning.
card_danny_flat_night_choice_stay_in_rea: The chat fills with photos from somebody’s kitchen.
card_app_referral_situation: The sign-up bonus cleared overnight: ◈25 paid for a friend who joined off your link. The referral page is one tap from the group chat, and two people there are asking what the app is.
card_app_referral_choice_post_label: Post the link in the chat
card_app_referral_choice_post_feedback: The link goes up and a second name joins by evening. The bonus is paid from the money that arrives after you, which is how the page can afford the first one.
card_app_referral_choice_post_reaction: The link is in the chat. One more name joins by evening.
card_app_referral_choice_stop_feedback: The first twenty-five is already yours, and the page keeps its own counsel. Nobody else gets the link, and the chat finds something else to talk about.
card_app_referral_choice_stop_reaction: The group chat argues about dinner instead.
card_referral_follow_up_situation: Three months on, the friend who took the link put fifty into the account and has thirty-eight left of it this morning. They ask whether you still use the app.
card_referral_follow_up_choice_square_fe: The bonus goes back across and the friend’s fifty is still down. The money moved, nothing changed for them, and twenty-five leaves your month.
card_referral_follow_up_choice_square_re: The twenty-five goes back and the message thread settles.
card_referral_follow_up_choice_explain_f: You send what the page says about how the bonus is paid and leave it there. The friend keeps the loss, and the answers they get are yours, not the app’s.
card_referral_follow_up_choice_explain_r: You type it out and the friend goes quiet for the night.
card_phone_shop_shift_situation: You pick up a Saturday at the phone shop. A mate walks in wanting the handset in the window; the four-payment plan is on the counter beside the till.
card_phone_shop_shift_choice_split_feedb: The forms take the hour and the mate leaves with the phone they came in for. Twenty in commission, and a third payment in a month they have not priced yet.
card_phone_shop_shift_choice_split_react: The application clears and the mate leaves with the bag.
card_phone_shop_shift_choice_outright_fe: The whole amount goes on the counter and the mate owes nobody. Ten instead of twenty for you, and no third payment waiting in their year.
card_phone_shop_shift_choice_outright_re: The mate counts the full amount onto the counter.
card_split_comes_due_situation: Three months on, the mate’s third payment lands in a week with nothing spare in it. The shop charges for a missed one, and the messages have gone short.
card_split_comes_due_choice_cover_feedba: Thirty covers what their week could not, and the payment lands on time. The phone stays on, and the shop’s fee for a missed one stays off their account.
card_split_comes_due_choice_cover_reacti: The transfer clears and the payment lands on its due day.
card_split_comes_due_choice_leave_feedba: The mate calls the shop and sorts it the slow way. The fee lands on their account, the phone stays on, and the messages stay short for a while.
card_split_comes_due_choice_leave_reacti: Their next message arrives a fortnight later, about something else.

epilogue_behind_study: Nineteen, and the course is still going, fitted around the shifts that pay for it. The debt runs past the loan the plan signed, and the months kept arriving anyway. That is where the five years left you; the course is still moving.

story_other_path_work: The other side of the Fork is the wage: the hours of the apprenticeship, and a Named Goal instead of a loan.
